# Use Gemini to plan a trip across multiple Google apps

> **In short:** Gemini can read your Gmail inbox to pull out flight confirmations and hotel bookings, suggest places to visit through Google Maps, and save a structured itinerary to Google Drive — all in one conversation. You'll need a Google account, the free Gemini app or website, and about 10 minutes to get started.

Picture this: you booked three flights, a hotel, and a rental car over the past six months, all through confirmation emails scattered across your inbox. Now you want one clear trip plan you can check on your phone before you leave. Gemini can dig through those emails, grab the key details, and put them into a document you can open anywhere. Here's how to make it happen step by step.

## Before you start

- A Google account (the same one you use for Gmail, Maps, and Drive). If you do not have one yet, go to [accounts.google.com](https://accounts.google.com) and create one — it is free.
- Gemini access. On a phone, download the **Gemini app** from the App Store or Google Play. On a computer, open a browser and go to **gemini.google.com** and sign in with your Google account. Gemini is currently available at no cost on most plans.
- At least one trip-related email in your Gmail (a flight confirmation, hotel booking, or event ticket).
- Basic comfort with typing a question and reading a reply. No technical experience needed.

Plan for about 10 minutes the first time you do this. It gets faster once you know the flow.

## Step 1 — Open Gemini and make sure it can see your Google apps

On your phone, open the **Gemini app** and look at the bottom of the screen. You should see a chat box with a blinking cursor, ready for your question. At the top, look for your account picture or initial — tap it to confirm you are signed into the Google account that holds your Gmail and Drive.

If you are on a computer, open **gemini.google.com** in Chrome, Firefox, or Edge. Sign in if prompted. You will see the same chat-style interface.

**What happens next:** A small notice may appear asking for permission to access your Google Workspace apps (Gmail, Drive, Maps). This is normal. Tap or click **Allow** so Gemini can read your emails and save documents to your Drive. Without this permission, Gemini cannot pull in trip details from Gmail or save your plan to Drive.

If you do not see a permission prompt, check the **Settings** (look for a gear icon in the corner) and look for something like "Connected apps" or "Extensions." Make sure Gmail and Drive are toggled on.

💬 Example: "Make sure Gemini can access your Google apps by checking Settings → Extensions → Google apps — then confirm Gmail and Drive are enabled."

You'll know it worked when the chat is ready and you can type a message, or when you have confirmed the extensions are on.

## Step 2 — Ask Gemini to find your trip emails in Gmail

Type a question in the chat box asking Gemini to look through your Gmail for trip-related emails. Be specific about what you want. Gemini will search your inbox, find matching emails, and pull out useful details like flight times, hotel addresses, and booking references.

A good question is direct and includes a time frame. For example, ask about a trip in a specific month or ask for all travel confirmations from the past year.

**What you see:** After you send the question, a short "Searching Gmail…" message appears. Within a few seconds, Gemini replies with a list of what it found. Each item shows the sender name, the subject line, and key details extracted from the email body — such as departure city, arrival city, flight times, hotel name, and address.

**What happens next:** Read through the reply. If something looks wrong or a booking is missing, tell Gemini. For example, say "That looks right, but I also have a hotel in Denver — can you check again?" Gemini will search again and update the list.

If you do not see any results and you are sure you have trip emails, the date range in your question might be too narrow. Try asking "Show me all travel confirmations from the last year" instead of just "my trip to Denver."

💬 Example: "Find all my flight and hotel confirmations from the past year in Gmail and list the key details — dates, times, addresses, and booking numbers."

You'll know it worked when Gemini replies with a list of your trip bookings, each showing at least a date, name, and one key detail like an address or confirmation number.

## Step 3 — Get location suggestions and directions from Google Maps

Once you have your flight and hotel details, ask Gemini to suggest places to visit near your destination or to give you directions from the airport to your hotel. Gemini can tap into Google Maps data to recommend restaurants, attractions, and routes without you needing to open the Maps app separately.

Ask in plain language. For example, ask about nearby attractions, the best route from the airport, or restaurant recommendations in a specific neighborhood.

**What you see:** Gemini replies with a text summary. If it includes an address or place name, you can tap or click it — a link usually appears that will open Google Maps directly to that location. You may see bullet points or a short paragraph listing suggestions with brief descriptions.

**What happens next:** You can follow the links to open Maps and save places to a list, or you can keep asking Gemini follow-up questions about the area. Gemini is reading from Maps data but does not replace the Maps app — for turn-by-turn directions, you will still open Maps.

If Gemini does not return specific place names and instead gives a vague answer like "there are many restaurants in that area," try narrowing your question. Specify a neighborhood or a type of food you want.

💬 Example: "What are the top three attractions within walking distance of the Grand Hyatt Denver? And what is the best route from Denver International Airport to that hotel?"

You'll know it worked when Gemini replies with named places, each tied to a specific address or neighborhood, and includes at least one clickable link that opens Google Maps.

## Step 4 — Ask Gemini to draft your itinerary and save it to Google Drive

Now bring everything together. Ask Gemini to write a day-by-day itinerary that includes your flight details from Step 2, the places to visit from Step 3, and any notes you want to add. Then ask it to save the result to Google Drive as a document you can open on your phone, tablet, or computer at any time.

Google Drive is a cloud storage service — think of it as a filing cabinet that lives online, so any document you save there is available on every device you sign into with the same Google account.

**What you see:** When you ask Gemini to save to Drive, it may show a preview of the document first. You should see a short note like "Saving to Drive…" followed by a confirmation. The document will appear in the root folder of your Google Drive, named something like "Trip Itinerary — Denver" or whatever title you asked for.

**What happens next:** Open your Drive (go to **drive.google.com** on a computer, or open the Drive app on your phone). Look for the file. Tap it to open and read. You can edit it, add notes, or share it with travel companions.

If Gemini says it cannot save to Drive, check that Drive is listed in the extensions (see Step 1) and that you have space available in your Drive account. Most free accounts get 15 gigabytes of storage, which is more than enough for text documents.

💬 Example: "Draft a day-by-day itinerary for my Denver trip from May 10 to May 14 using the flight and hotel details you found. Include the airport-to-hotel route, my three attractions, and dinner suggestions each evening. Save it to Google Drive as 'Denver Trip Plan'."

You'll know it worked when you can open Google Drive, find a new document with your trip name, and see the itinerary laid out with dates, times, and addresses.

## Step 5 — Open your itinerary on the go

Before you leave, open the saved document on your phone so you have it ready offline or on a weak Wi-Fi connection. In Google Drive, tap the document, then look for a download or save icon — often a cloud with a downward arrow. This saves a copy to your device's storage so you can read it without an internet connection.

On a computer, open the document and press **Ctrl+P** (Windows) or **Cmd+P** (Mac) to print it as a PDF, which you can save locally.

**What you see:** A PDF or offline copy saved to your phone's Files or Downloads folder. You can also share the link directly from Drive by tapping the Share button — this sends a link to anyone you choose, so your travel companion or family can see the plan too.

**What happens next:** Keep the document or PDF handy. When you land, open your Maps app for navigation, and keep the itinerary open for reference. If anything changes — a delayed flight, a new restaurant — open Gemini again and ask it to update the Drive document.

If you cannot find the downloaded file on your phone, check the Files app (iPhone) or Downloads folder (Android). Searching "Denver" in your file manager often finds it quickly.

💬 Example: "Download my 'Denver Trip Plan' document from Drive so I can read it without Wi-Fi, then share the link with my travel companion."

You'll know it worked when the document opens offline or you receive a notification that the share link was sent successfully.

## Common mistakes

- **Asking too vaguely.** "Find my travel stuff" might return nothing useful. Be specific: "Find all emails with 'flight confirmation' or 'hotel booking' from the last six months." Specific questions get specific answers.
- **Forgetting to allow app access.** If Gemini says it cannot read your emails or save to Drive, go back to Settings and confirm the Gmail and Drive extensions are turned on. Gemini cannot access those apps without your permission.
- **Not checking the itinerary before you travel.** Gemini pulls details accurately in most cases, but confirmation numbers and dates can sometimes be off by a day if the email format is unusual. Read through the saved document before you leave and fix anything that looks wrong.

## What this means for you

- **In everyday life:** You no longer need to dig through months of emails to remember which hotel you booked or what time your return flight leaves. Gemini finds it all and puts it in one place, so you spend less time organizing and more time looking forward to the trip.
- **For your business or work:** If you travel for work, keep all receipts and itineraries in one Drive folder. Gemini can pull your conference hotel and flight details from your inbox so you arrive prepared, with directions and schedule in one document you can hand to an assistant.
- **If you are just getting started:** Your very first move is the easiest — open Gemini, type a question about one trip email you know you have, and see what it finds. That single step proves the connection works, and everything else builds from there.

## Try it now

Open Gemini (on your phone or at **gemini.google.com**), make sure you are signed in, and ask it to find your most recent travel confirmation email. Type: "Find my most recent flight or hotel confirmation in Gmail and tell me the dates and confirmation number." Then look at the reply. That's it — you have just had Gemini read your inbox for trip information. From here, you are ready to ask for more details, add places to visit, and build your itinerary.
